title: Failing join test and the in-memory thinking registry
goal: A committed failing test expects a model call to show as a live thinking entry and to vanish when the call ends
acceptance: A failing test (committed first) starts a planner call, a consultant call and a Casper check against a fake model in a temporary home and expects the service's thinking snapshot to list each while it runs and to be empty after it ends, on success, on a model error and on a timeout; today no such state exists
Each entry carries pilot name (the same name the sortie line shows, e.g. Maya), role (planner, consultant, Casper), model, sortie ID and the start time; no prompt text, no answer text

A plain TypeScript module in src/ (no framework imports) holds the registry: begin returns a handle, end is idempotent, a stuck entry expires after a ceiling so a crashed call never shows thinking forever; unit tests for begin, end, double end, expiry and invalid input
privacy: Neutral invented pilots, sorties and models only; no owner data or tokens in Git, tests or logs.
escalation: A material scope or effort increase goes to the owner
A visible change in how a section looks or behaves goes to the owner

effort.basis: Estimated 2026-11-26: one small registry module, its unit tests and the failing join test. Not a measurement.
